newsitem.title: UK: UK shares stay higher, await Wall Street lead.
newsitem.headline: UK shares stay higher, await Wall Street lead.

text.p: UK shares were moderately higher on Thursday as investors continued to take a more relaxed view about the outlook for interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic following the U.S. central bank's decision Tuesday to leave rates unchanged.
But weak U.S. Treasuries are expected to weigh on U.S stocks today which could put pressure on UK blue chips later in the session, dealer said.
"It looks like Wall Street might have a bit of a bumpy start if bond yields keep rising. That won't help our market," one senior dealer said. The FTSE 100 was up 12.4 points to 4,654.4.
Trading volume on the top 100 constituents by 1305 GMT was around 460 million shares with advancers outpacing decliners by 52 to 39 with nine unchanged.

Although the U.S. Federal Reserve chose not to push up its key short-term funds rate this week, most market participants believe higher rates are inevitable in both the U.S. and the UK in order to prevent an inflationary spike.

Talk of higher rates swirled around London dealing rooms on Thursday after news that April retail sales had risen a monthly 0.1 percent and yearly 4.7 percent against expectations of a monthly 0.3 percent and a yearly 4.1 percent.
Meanwhile, first quarter GDP rose 0.9 percent quarterly and three percent yearly versus expectations of 1.0 percent quarterly and matching expectations of three percent yearly.

"Although April retail sales were on the soft side of expectations, revisions have boosted annual growth to a very robust 4.7 pct. This should be seen as increasing the likelihood that the Bank of England will hike rates soon unless the budget is very tight," said Bank of America's Jeremy Hawkins.
Strategists noted that consumer spending at market prices rose one percent.

"We are coming from too strong a base to be able to absorb the pick-up in spending we will see in the summer without generating inflationary pressure," said Charterhouse group chief economist, Richard Jeffrey, referring to windfall gains for consumers from upcoming building society flotations.
Dealers said most participants had discounted higher UK interest rates and were now concentrating on how Wall Street performed over the coming weeks.
"The Dow has taken our market to new highs this month. It is still the only game in town at the moment," the head of trading at a major brokerage said.

With the yield on the benchmark U.S. 30-year long bond once again threatening to push above the seven percent level -- a point where bonds can become more attractive to investors than equities -- the Dow may suffer a few weak sessions, dealers said.
The long bond was down 5/32 to 95-20/32, yielding 6.98 percent. The June long gilt future eased 18/32 to 112-12/32.

Reed International Plc dropped 16p to 609-1/2 after Merrill Lynch analysts downgraded the stock, and a U.S. press report raised concerns about the group's U.S. legal publishing unit Lexis-Nexis, dealers said.
Storehouse Plc gained 7-1/2p to 224 after a bullish current trading statement and in-line, full-year profits.
B.A.T Industries Plc put on 10-1/2p to 569 as a U.S. court ruling dealt a blow to attempts by U.S. states to sue tobacco companies for healthcare costs.

B.A.T unit Brown & Williamson said a Maryland judge had dismissed nine of 13 counts by the state to recover Medicaid expenditures from it, ruling that it does not have a right to recover Medicaid payments made on behalf of individual smokers.
Near-term support for the FTSE 100 was pegged at 4,610 with resistance seen at 4,666, technical analysts said.
--Dale Faulken, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
